edits.english: A dilemma was raised before the Sages: If the court issued a ruling that forbidden fat is permitted, and a minority of the congregation performed the transgression of eating forbidden fat on the basis of that ruling, and the court reversed its initial decision, but then reversed itself again and issued a ruling that forbidden fat is permitted, and a different minority of the congregation performed the transgression, what is the halakha? The Gemara elaborates: Is it that since there are two disparate experiences of awareness, the first minority does not combine with the second minority, even though the two minorities together would constitute a majority? Or perhaps, since both this transgression and that transgression are the same, eating forbidden fat, the first minority combines with the second minority, and the two minorities together constitute a majority.

edits.hebrew: או דלמא - כיון דחלב שם אחד הוא, דבין חלב המכסה את הקרב ובין חלב המכסה את הדקין שם אחד הוא, שחלב סתם איקרו:

edits.english: And further, a dilemma was raised before them [the Sages]: If the court issued a ruling that forbidden fat is permitted, and a minority of the congregation performed the transgression of eating fat on the basis of their ruling, and the court reversed their initial ruling, but afterward they reversed themselves again and issued a ruling to permit it, and then a different minority performed the transgression on the basis of their ruling, what is the halakha? The two sides of the question are: Is it that since there are two separate instances of awareness, the first minority does not combine with the second minority, even though these two minorities together constitute a majority of the congregation? Or perhaps, since both this transgression and that transgression are the prohibition of eating forbidden fat, they combine?

And if you say in that case: Since both this transgression and that transgression are the same, eating forbidden fat, the first minority combines with the second minority, then there is another dilemma: In a case where a minority performed a transgression on the basis of the first ruling of the court and ate forbidden fat that is upon the stomach, and a minority performed a transgression on the basis of the second ruling of the court and ate forbidden fat that is upon the small intestines, what is the halakha? The Gemara elaborates: Here, certainly, since these transgressions come from two different verses, the first minority does not combine with the second minority; or perhaps, since both this transgression and that transgression are the same, eating forbidden fat, the first minority combines with the second minority, and the two minorities together constitute a majority.

And if you say: Since both this transgression and that transgression are the prohibition of eating forbidden fat, they combine, then there is room for the following dilemma: If there was a minority that erred based on one ruling of the court regarding fat that is upon the stomach, and a minority that erred based on another ruling regarding fat that is upon the small intestines, what is the halakha? The two sides of this question are: Here, certainly, since these come from two verses, as each type of fat has a different source in the Torah, the first minority does not combine; or perhaps, since both this transgression and that transgression are the prohibition of eating forbidden fat, and they are included in one prohibition, they combine?

edits.hebrew: הורו בית דין שחלב המכסה את הקרב כו' - תימה, דאמרינן לקמן (הוריות ד.) אין בית דין חייבין עד שיורו בדבר שאין הצדוקין מודין; ובשלמא חלב שעל הדקין דאתי מריבויה (חולין מט) ניחא, דאין הצדוקין מודין בו; אלא חלב המכסה את הקרב וכן דם, מאי איכא למימר? מיהו לפי התוספתא דמכילתין ניחא, דתנא לקיים מצות חייבין כיצד יש חלב ודם בתורה, אבל אין חייבין אלא על הקרב לשלמים. ואף על גב דדם חיה נאסר, שמא הצדוקים אומרים דגם הוא קרב:

edits.english: And if you say in that case: It is the name of forbidden fat that they both have in common, and the first minority combines with the second minority, then there is another dilemma: In a case where a minority performed a transgression on the basis of the first ruling of the court and ate forbidden fat, and a minority performed a transgression on the basis of the second ruling of the court and ate forbidden blood, what is the halakha? The Gemara elaborates: Here, certainly, they are two distinct prohibitions, and since the nature of their prohibition is not identical, the first minority does not combine with the second minority. Or perhaps, since their offerings are identical, as one is liable to bring a sin-offering for unwitting violation of either of these prohibitions, the first minority combines with the second minority.

edits.hebrew: כיון דתרי איסורי נינהו - דחלב אינו שוה בכל, דחלב חיה מותר:
או דלמא - כיון דאילו ציבור אכלי האי חלב והאי דם שלא בהוראה בשגגת מעשה, מייתו כל חד וחד, אי בעו כשבה מייתו אי בעו שעירה מייתו, דמצי אשוויי קרבנם; השתא נמי כי עשו בהוראה מצטרפי:

edits.english: And if you say: It is the name 'fat' and it combines, then there is room for the following dilemma: If a minority of the congregation erred based on a court ruling regarding forbidden fat, and a minority erred based on a ruling regarding forbidden blood, what is the halakha? The two sides of this question are: Here, certainly, since they are two different prohibitions, and since their prohibition is not identical, they do not combine. Or perhaps, since their offerings are identical, as for both of them one brings a sin-offering, they combine?

edits.hebrew: וחזרו והורו שדם מותר - הא דקתני כהאי גוונא, דמשמע דוקא משום שידעו בינתים שטעו בחלב; דהא אפילו לא ידעו נמי מצינן למבעי כדקאמר, משום דשני מינים הם, דם שוה בכל ולא חלב, אלא נקטינן אגב אחריני. והא דלא פשיט מההוא דלעיל עד שיהיו כולן בשגגה אחת, דהכא כיון דתליא בבית דין הוי שגגה אחת:

edits.english: And if you say in that case: Since their offerings are identical, the first minority combines with the second minority, then there is another dilemma: In a case where a minority performed a transgression on the basis of the first ruling of the court and ate forbidden fat, and a minority performed a transgression on the basis of the second ruling of the court and engaged in idol worship, what is the halakha? Here, certainly, neither are their prohibitions identical nor are their offerings identical, because an individual who unwittingly engages in idol worship may bring only a female goat for atonement. Therefore, the first minority does not combine with the second minority. Or perhaps, since for both this transgression and that transgression one is liable to receive excision from the World-to-Come [karet] if he performs it intentionally, the first minority combines with the second minority. The Gemara concludes: The dilemma shall stand unresolved.

edits.hebrew: ומיעוט בתרא בעבודת כוכבים - קרבנם שעירה ולא כשבה:

edits.english: And if you say: Since their offerings are identical, they combine, another dilemma will arise: If there was a minority that erred based on a ruling regarding forbidden fat, and a different minority that erred regarding idol worship, what is the halakha? The two sides of this question are: Here, certainly, neither are their prohibitions identical nor are their offerings identical, because even an individual who unwittingly engages in idol worship must bring a she-goat specifically for his atonement, so the minorities do not combine. Or perhaps, since both this transgression and that transgression are an offense for which one is liable to receive karet if performed intentionally, there is still a commonality between them, and they combine? These questions were not resolved and the dilemma shall stand unresolved.

edits.hebrew: והורו שעבודת כוכבים מותרת - צריך עיון מה יביאו, כיון שאין קרבנותיהן שוין, אם יביאו קרבן עבודת כוכבים וגם דחלב או לא? וגם צריך עיון אי דוקא מיבעיא דמעיקרא הוי מיעוט וכן בסוף, אבל אי הוי רובו בסוף לא איצטרכי למיעוטא שיתכפר בפר לההוא מיעוטא. איכא דאמרי לא שנא, אבל הא ודאי אי הוי מתחלה רובא ולבסוף מיעוטא, אין מיעוט מצטרף לרובא כיון שכבר נתחייבו רובא בקרבן:
